groups.name: Scaling laws for language models
groups.dimension: how the compute-optimal split between model size and training tokens is estimated
groups.comparison: Kaplan et al. fit power laws with one fixed training schedule; Clark et al. extend the fits to routed (MoE) models; neither varies the training horizon per model

groups.name: Large dense language models
groups.dimension: parameter count vs. number of training tokens at a given budget
groups.comparison: GPT-3, Gopher and MT-NLG grow parameters (175B to 530B) while keeping training data around 300B tokens

gaps.statement: Existing compute-optimal estimates were fitted with a single training schedule, so the effect of the number of training tokens on the optimal model size was never measured directly.

contributions.text: We train over 400 language models from 70 million to over 16 billion parameters on 5 to 500 billion tokens, each with a schedule matched to its training horizon, and estimate the compute-optimal frontier with three independent approaches.
All three approaches predict that model size and training tokens should be scaled in equal proportions.

evidence.quote: Estimated parameter and data scaling with increased training compute

contributions.text: We train Chinchilla, a 70B-parameter model on 1.4 trillion tokens with the Gopher compute budget; it reaches 67.6% average accuracy on MMLU, 7.6% above Gopher.

author_notes: Source conflict: the abstract (p1) reports 67.5% MMLU accuracy, Section 4.2.2 and Table 6 (p11) report 67.6%; the draft uses the Table 6 value - confirm with the authors.
